newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes pre-selling of phosphate to save firm.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes pre-selling of phosphate to save firm.

text.p: The Philippine Phosphate Fertiliser Corp (Philphos) is planning to pre-sell about $500 million worth of its output to retire part of its $1.4 billion debt, Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said on Friday.
Philphos is partly owned by state investment firm, the National Development Corp, where Bautista sits as chairman.
Bautista said the $500 million worth of phosphate represents 50 percent of the company's projected output in the next five years.
The Japanese government, who is one of its main creditors, might be interested in making the advance payment, he said.
"This is not a purely altruistic move on their part ... If Philphos were to close shop, prices in the world market will increase," he told reporters.
Philphos produces about a million tonnes of fertiliser every year, 70 percent of which is for export.
